tldr: A 2-hour hands-on lab building an end-to-end ML pipeline in pure Java using JTaccuino notebooks, Hardwood, DFLib, DeepNetts and an early look at gog4j.
summary: Sven Reimers and Zoran Sevarac's lab challenges the idea that data science requires switching to Python. Participants build a complete predictive machine learning pipeline entirely on the JVM, working interactively in code.

The stack includes JTaccuino for Jupyter-style notebooks, Hardwood as a zero-dependency Apache Parquet reader, DFLib for data frame cleaning and manipulation, and DeepNetts for building, training and evaluating neural networks on CPU or GPU. Attendees also get a first look at gog4j, an unreleased plotting API based on the grammar of graphics.
keyPoints: Complete ML pipeline built without leaving Java.
Hardwood reads Parquet; DFLib handles data frames.
DeepNetts trains neural networks with CPU or GPU acceleration.
gog4j is an unreleased grammar-of-graphics plotting API.
takeaways: Try DFLib and a Java notebook for your next data exploration task.
watchIf: You are a Java developer curious about data science and machine learning without switching to Python.
